content.text: The cause is the shell, not room-3. `shell.mjs` fills every interior cell of the main block with air (`box()`, y3..17), and `runParts` records air as owned. So every cell of the dining room is locked before this part runs. I'll confirm the palette side too, since refused writes never reach the off-palette check.

input.summary:
room: dining room is now clean in make.sh (0 placed, no REFUSED, no OFF-PALETTE); build.nbt written with the part present but empty.
The planned furniture (table, 10 chairs, barrel sideboard, 5 chain-and-lantern pairs) was dropped because the shell owns every interior cell.
All 7 block ids the part used are in palette.json, so the off-palette check had nothing to fix.
left: The dining room is empty in build.nbt. The 46 furniture writes were refused, so nothing was placed. To restore it: a table of dark_oak_fence at y4 and dark_oak_slab (top) at y5 along z44, x56..66; 10 dark_oak_stairs chairs at y4 on z43 (facing north) and z45 (facing south), x57..65 odd; barrels at x68 z43..45 y4 with a lit candle at (68,5,44); iron_chain plus hanging lantern pairs at (61,44), (53,44), (54,48), (59,48), (67,48). The original code is in git history of this file if it was tracked; the header comment carries the layout.

Systemic, not fixed here (outside room-3.mjs): shell.mjs box() fills every interior cell of the main block (x27..68, z43..60, y3..17) with air, and runParts locks air the shell wrote. Any room part that furnishes inside the main block is refused. Refused counts in this run: entrance hall 42, parlour library 64, butler's pantry 24, powder room 23, kitchen 31, bedroom 3 28, bedroom 5 21, bedroom 6 21, ground gallery 2, cottage bath 2, gazebo 4, greenhouse 7. The fix belongs in the shell or the lock policy (leave room interiors unowned, or run furnishers before the shell's air fill), not in the room parts.
Lock ownership is not reported. The refusal says 'had air' but not which part owns the cell, so the cause took source reading to find.

waste.what: Finding out which earlier part locked the dining-room cells. The refusal line only says 'had air'; I read runParts and shell.mjs to find the box() air fill.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls reading build.mjs and shell.mjs
waste.tool: runParts refusal report should name the owning part per cell (for example 'owned by shell.mjs box()'). The existing MCD_PARTS_CELLS env var already records each part's cells; a `mcd plan`-style map of locked cells per room box would show this before any writes.

waste.what: Checking OFF-PALETTE by hand. Refused writes never reach the palette check, so the report stayed silent about this part's blocks. I ran a node snippet to test the 7 block ids against palette.json.
waste.tool: runParts should check palette membership for every attempted write, before the lock check. Or `mcd blocks --check` could run over the part's block ids automatically.

companions.task: Refit the dining-room furniture (table, chairs, sideboard, chandelier) once the shell stops owning the interior air, and check it with mcd fit and mcd room against rooms.json.
Change the shell's interior air fill, or the lock policy, so that room furnishers can write into the main block's rooms. This is the fix that unblocks all 12 refused room parts.
